description: Require npm dependency version specifiers to be pinned to an exact resolved version, not a floating range, dist-tag, or unpinned git/URL ref.
appliesTo: package.json dependencies, devDependencies, optionalDependencies, and peerDependencies — checked at add/bump time (check-dependency, package-json-guard) and on existing trees (scan-dependencies)

policy.description: A version specifier must resolve to exactly one immutable artifact: a bare exact semver, or a git/URL ref pinned to a commit SHA. Ranges, dist-tags, and mutable refs are rejected.
policy.rationale: npm supply-chain attacks — event-stream (2018, a compromised transitive maintainer add slipped in via a normal minor bump) and ua-parser-js (2021, malicious versions published directly to existing tags and pulled in wherever a caret range like ^0.7.29 was declared) — land through auto-resolved floating ranges silently pulling a newly compromised release at install time, often executing via a postinstall script with no review of the new bytes. An exact pin means a compromised release sits unused until someone deliberately bumps the version, ideally through this plugin's OSV + license gate.
policy.exceptions: None by default. A temporary range must be documented in the PR and re-pinned before merge.

pinned: Bare exact semver (4.17.21, prerelease/build metadata allowed)
git/URL ref with a commit-SHA (7-40 hex chars) after '#'
floating: git/URL ref with a branch, non-SHA tag, or no ref

exemptPrefixes.note: Reported for awareness, never failed on — these are not fetched from the public registry the same way this policy's threat model targets.
exemptPrefixes.alsoExempt: Bare relative/absolute local paths used without an explicit file: prefix

severity._peerDependenciesNote: peerDependencies declare a compatibility RANGE by design — npm never installs a peerDependency on the declaring package's behalf, so a broad range there is idiomatic, not a floating-install risk. Report for visibility; never fail.
